provenance: New synthetic confirmation case, authored after v5 stability failures and sealed before v6 inference; not a population-random sample.
transcript:
[00:00] Speaker1: This dataset has 240 rows, but 18 are duplicates. That doesn't prove there are 222 distinct patients; one patient can have several valid rows.
[00:10] Speaker2: I cleaned the label spelling yesterday, not the duplicate rows.
[00:20] Speaker3: Shall we delete the duplicates now?
[00:30] Speaker1: No deletion is approved. Make a reversible copy for inspection first.
[00:40] Speaker2: I'll make that copy by noon tomorrow. My audio cut out before my name; keep my label as Speaker2.
[00:50] Speaker3: The directory says Morgan.
[01:00] Speaker2: That's the lab account, not my name.
[01:10] Speaker1: I am Dana. I will inspect the copy after it exists, but I am not committing to tomorrow.
[01:20] Speaker3: The preliminary analysis says 62 percent. Is that accuracy?
[01:30] Dana: No. That's the fraction of labeled rows, not a validated model accuracy.
[01:40] Speaker2: We proposed releasing the dataset at the end of this quarter.
[01:50] Dana: That remains only a proposal. Consent approval is still missing; do not publish until it is granted.
[02:00] Speaker3: Can we say all consent forms are lost?
[02:10] Dana: No, missing approval does not establish lost forms. We don't know their status yet.
[02:20] Speaker2: Is external review funded?
[02:30] Dana: Not decided. The old 900-dollar allocation belongs to a different project.
